### Investment Memo: IT (Gartner, Inc.) — 24 October 2026

**Verdict**: HOLD — pass on new capital at $219.64; hold existing positions small | **Conviction**: Medium
**Price Target**: $245 (~+12% from $219.64) — blended from Value's probability-weighted $253 intrinsic, Growth's $240 trim trigger, and the short-desk's $290 bull / $160 bear symmetry
**Time Horizon**: 12–24 months

---

**Investment Thesis**

Gartner is a high-quality, cash-generative franchise (70% gross margin, ~$1.2B FCF, ~160% FCF conversion, negative accruals) caught in a structural re-pricing of its business model: the market believes generative AI commoditizes syndicated research, and contract value (CV) growth of ~1.7–2.5% — against 3.7% CPI and shrinking client count (−4.5%) — is the live evidence. The stock has already absorbed the punishment (−72% peak-to-trough) and recovered 75% off the June low to a fair-to-full ~15x FY26E adjusted EPS. What remains is a genuinely bimodal name: if CV re-accelerates above 3–5% on AI-governance demand, a re-rating toward $275–290 follows; if CV stalls below 2% or turns negative, the multiple compresses toward $150–165. At the current price, above the sell-side median target and days before a binary Q3 print, the risk/reward is symmetric — not actionable.

---

**Key Findings by Domain**

- **Macro & Sector**: End-market demand is superb (global IT spend +14.2% to $6.37T; AI +49.5%) but the benefit bypasses research budgets — CIO budgets guided only +3.7% for 2027, i.e. zero real growth against 3.7% CPI. Rising real yields (10Y TIPS 2.80%) and a +3% USD are mild headwinds; the multiple damage is largely paid. Sector = mature oligopoly in early structural disruption: Gartner is the last direct comp standing (Forrester revenue −17% over two years, 0.5% op margin; Clarivate loss-making). **Both agents: NEUTRAL.**
- **Geopolitical & Legal**: MEDIUM risk. Live securities class action (*Schmidt v. Gartner*, class period Feb-2025–Feb-2026) attacking CV disclosure, plus a probable derivative suit; US federal budget cuts were the specific cause of the 2025 CV break; 26% EMEA exposure carries EU AI Act/GDPR load. No sanctions/FCPA/enforcement actions currently active.
- **Value**: **HOLD.** Narrow, narrowing moat (ROIC 26–33% vs ~9% WACC, but CV ~1–2% and FY26 revenue guided −1.8%). Intrinsic ~$253 (bear $129 / base $286 / bull $342); 13% discount is short of the 25–30% margin of safety required. Buy below ~$180; trim above ~$290.
- **Growth**: **HOLD.** Rule of 40 = 22; forward revenue growth ~3–4%; 13% EPS growth is substantially buyback math (share count −23% since 2021). Add at $170–180 or on CV >3%; trim above $240 without a credible FY27 guide.
- **Quantitative Signals**: **NEUTRAL.** Cheapest in peer set (value score 1/4) with decent-but-deteriorating quality (ROIC 33%→26%), but 12–1 momentum −23.5%, 62% annualized volatility, beta 0.31 with R²=0.005 (risk is idiosyncratic, not market). Price sits above the mean ($192) and median ($190) analyst target.
- **Financial Risk**: **MODERATE.** Credit is fine — net leverage 1.1–1.5x, interest coverage 9–14x, no maturity wall. Equity risk is high — negative book equity (−$167M), buybacks ($3.1B over 18 months) exceed FCF (~$1.9B), 56–62% vol, −77% cycle drawdown. Bonds fine; stock not.
- **Non-Financial Risk**: **HIGH** — the binding constraint. Governance/disclosure is the attack surface: combined CEO/Chair (22-year CEO), CLO resigning mid-litigation (effective 16-Oct-2026), 2023 FCPA controls precedent, two corrective disclosures on the same metric (CV) each triggering 20%+ single-day losses.
- **ESG**: **AVERAGE / NEUTRAL.** Environmentally immaterial (asset-light). Weak pillar is Governance: stale board (several 20–36-year tenures), Chair/CEO duality, 82% PSU payout and 119.6% bonus in a −23% TSR year with targets re-cut to exclude the federal business. Research-independence ("pay-to-play") critique is the one ESG issue that is load-bearing for the thesis.
- **Alternative Data**: **BULLISH into the print, poor entry.** 7/7 consecutive beats (avg +13%), Q2 CV accelerating (+0.3% q/q), NCVI positive, UBS channel check above consensus (CV +2.5% vs 2.3%), stable sales hiring. But the stock is +12% in four sessions into the event — the beat is likely priced.
- **Short / Contrarian**: **NO EDGE — reject short.** Earnings quality is high (Beneish −2.877, negative accruals every year, receivables shrinking, OCF/NI 1.77x). Forensic red flags are real (price-led CV on a shrinking client base, cost-cut-driven margin recovery, unaudited CV metric) but the mispricing has been harvested at ~14x EV/FCF with no solvency risk.

---

**Bull Case**
- **CV inflection confirmed**: two consecutive quarters of acceleration, a channel check above consensus, and AI-governance/EU AI Act demand could push CV back to mid-single digits — a re-rating to 17–20x on $16–17 EPS yields $275–300.
- **Financial engineering floor**: ~$2B/yr of buybacks against a ~$14B cap is a ~13% annual share-count shrink, manufacturing double-digit EPS growth even at flat revenue, funded by a ~9% FCF yield.
- **Last-man-standing franchise**: >50% share, 16x nearest pure-play rival, Magic Quadrant network effects, conferences compounding +15% at ~60% contribution margin, and AI complexity *raising* demand for credentialed judgment.

**Bear Case**
- **AI substitution is already in the numbers**: CV ~2%, client count −4.5%, growth manufactured by price on a shrinking base — the classic late-stage subscription signature. If CV turns negative, there is no valuation floor before ~$150.
- **Margin cliff in 2027**: the 2026 margin recovery (22.6% in Q2) is cost cuts masking a declining top line; you can only cut once, and FY24/FY25/FY26 earnings are distorted by one-offs in both directions.
- **Governance/litigation overhang**: a validated class action on the exact metric anchoring valuation, a CLO exit mid-case, and buybacks executed at $300–450 into a decelerating core (~$1B+ of value destroyed) — a negative-equity balance sheet with no cushion if the narrative breaks again.

**Key Risks**
1. **Q3 print (3 Nov)** — binary event; the stock has gapped ±20%+ on two of the last three prints. Watch CV growth, net new CV, and client count — not the EPS beat.
2. **CV <2% for two quarters or client count <12,500** — confirms structural decline; exit.
3. **Feb-2027 FY27 guidance** — the event that caused a −21% day in Feb-2026; pattern of disappointing guides not yet broken.
4. **Legal escalation** — derivative suit naming directors, SEC inquiry into AI disclosures, or evidence the CLO departure relates to disclosure controls.
5. **Buyback pause** — removes the sole EPS engine and the price floor.
6. **Macro bear tail** — Warsh-Fed hikes into 3.7% CPI, 10Y through 5.5% → $150–165 retest.

**Portfolio Construction Note**
Target **1.0%**, hard cap **1.5%**, and **do not initiate at $219.64**. Conditional 0.5% starter only after Q3 confirms CV ≥2.5–3% with the guide intact; add to 1.0–1.25% at $180–190 or on CV >3% with a credible FY27 outlook. Hard stop $160–165 (closing basis — 62% vol makes intraday stops noise). Trim one-third at $240–250 without a CV >3% print, half at $255–265, exit ~$290+. IT correlates 0.07 with SPY but 0.58–0.68 with FDS/MORN/VRSK — it is a market diversifier but an information-services concentrator; do not stack it on an existing data-analytics bucket. Low beta is an illusion: risk here is event-driven, so position size, not beta, is the control.

---

**Dissent & data gaps flagged**: Agents split cleanly — Alt Data (near-term bullish) vs. Sector/Value/Growth (structurally cautious); Non-Fin Risk's HIGH rating overrides Value's modest discount in sizing. Peer multiples were unavailable (FMP's "Technology" peer set returns mega-cap semis — non-comparable); the 10-K legal-proceedings note, DEF 14A, debt maturity schedule, and insider transaction direction could not be retrieved from primary filings; FY24 EPS ($16.00) and FY25 EBITDA contain one-offs that flatter then depress comparisons — normalized EPS growth since 2024 is low single digits, not the +50% headline recovery.

*Bottom line: a good business at a fair price with a bad entry point and a live governance overhang. Buy the confirmation or the pullback — not the narrative.*

# Portfolio Construction Recommendation — Gartner, Inc. (NYSE: IT)

**Price:** $219.64 (20-Oct-2026 close) · **Market cap:** ~$13.9B–$15.8B depending on share-count convention · **EV:** ~$16.1B–$17.7B · **Next catalyst:** Q3-2026 results, 3-Nov-2026

---

## 1. Agent Conviction Summary Table

| Agent | View | Conviction | Key Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sector Researcher** | Neutral on information services; Gartner is best-in-class within a threatened niche | Medium | IT spend is booming (+14.2% to $6.37T), but Gartner’s contract value growth has stalled at ~2.5%. The business model, not the end market, is the problem. |
| **Geo Legal Researcher** | Medium risk (low end) | Medium | Live securities class action plus probable derivative action; US federal budget exposure; 26% EMEA concentration. No sanctions/FCPA issues currently active. |
| **Macro Researcher** | Neutral, mildly unfavourable | Medium | Real yields at 2.80%, CPI 3.72%, USD +3%, CIO budgets guided +3.7% for 2027. Macro is a 1–2% revenue headwind and mild multiple headwind — not a thesis-breaker. |
| **Value Researcher** | **Hold** | Medium | Narrow/narrowing moat. Probability-weighted intrinsic value ~$253; stock is a ~13% discount, short of the 25–30% margin of safety required. Buy below ~$180; trim above ~$290. |
| **Growth Researcher** | **Hold** | Medium | Rule of 40 = 22; revenue guided down 1–2% in FY26; CV +1.7% FX-neutral. EPS growth is substantially buyback math. Add at $170–180 or on CV >3%; trim above $240 without a 2027 guide. |
| **Fin Risk Analyst** | **Moderate financial risk** | High (risk assessment) | Net leverage 1.1–1.5x, interest coverage 9–14x, FCF ~$1.2B. But negative book equity (−$167M), buybacks exceed FCF, and 56–62% equity volatility. Credit is fine; equity risk is high. |
| **Non-Fin Risk Analyst** | **High risk** | High | Governance/disclosure is the binding risk: active securities fraud class action, CLO resignation effective 16-Oct-2026, combined CEO/Chair, 2023 FCPA controls precedent. |
| **Quant Analyst** | **Neutral / speculative buy only** | Medium | Value score attractive (1 of 4 peers), quality decent but deteriorating, 12-1 momentum −23.5%, volatility 61.9%, beta 0.31 with R² 0.005. Not a factor-model buy. |
| **Short Analyst** | **No edge — reject short thesis** | High | Earnings quality high; Beneish M-score −2.877; negative accruals; receivables shrinking. The bear case has largely been paid out at ~14x EV/FCF. |
| **ESG Analyst** | **Average / neutral** | Medium | Environmental risk low. Governance is the weak pillar: stale board, CEO/Chair duality, pay-for-performance optics. No ESG-driven exclusion or re-rating. |
| **Alt Data Analyst** | **Bullish near-term, unfavourable entry** | Medium | 7/7 earnings beats, CV accelerating, sales hiring stable, UBS channel check above consensus. But stock is +75% off the low and above median analyst target. |

---

## 2. Consensus Assessment

**Agreement level: SPLIT** — medium agreement on business quality, low agreement on entry timing and valuation.

### What the agents agree on

1. **Gartner is a high-quality cash generator, not a fraud or solvency risk.** The Short Analyst’s forensic work is explicit: earnings quality is high, accruals are negative, receivables are shrinking, and the Beneish M-score shows no manipulation signature. Fin Risk confirms leverage is manageable and there is no near-term maturity wall.
2. **The stock is no longer expensive on cash flow.** At ~15–16x FY26E adjusted EPS, ~12–14x EV/EBITDA, and a 7.4%–9% FCF yield, the easy “short the AI casualty” trade is gone. The Short Analyst rejects a fresh short.
3. **No agent recommends chasing at $219.64.** Value and Growth both say HOLD with buy zones of ~$170–180. The stock is above the median sell-side target (~$189–200) after a +75% rebound from the June low.
4. **The Nov 3 print is a binary near-term event.** Alt Data is bullish on the fundamentals into the quarter, but explicitly warns the entry point is poor. The stock has moved ±20% on two of the last three prints.

### Where the agents disagree

- **Near-term vs. structural:** Alt Data sees a beat-and-raise setup; Sector, Value, Growth and Macro see a decelerating, AI-threatened subscription franchise whose terminal value is being repriced.
- **Valuation vs. risk:** Value sees a 13% discount to intrinsic value; Non-Fin Risk sees HIGH governance/litigation risk and Fin Risk sees 60%+ volatility. The discount is real but not large enough to compensate for the risk stack.
- **Quality vs. momentum:** Quant likes value and quality but flags negative 12-1 momentum and the worst-in-class low-vol score. This is a value/quality stock with event-stock risk.

### Conflict resolution

The **Non-Financial Risk HIGH rating and the Geo Legal MEDIUM rating take precedence over the Value/Growth HOLD views** when sizing. Fraud risk is low, but litigation and disclosure-control risk are live and directly attack the metric — contract value — on which the entire thesis depends. The Value Researcher’s own conclusion supports this: a 13% discount is not enough. The Alt Data bullish signal is real but tactical; it does not change the portfolio-level risk budget.

**Aggregated conviction: ~4.5–5.0 / 10.** Good business, fair-to-full price, high idiosyncratic risk, no margin of safety, binary catalyst. This is a small-position-or-wait name, not a core holding.

---

## 3. Position Sizing Recommendation

### Recommended sizing

| Item | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| **Target position size** | **1.0% of portfolio** |
| **Maximum position size** | **1.5%** |
| **Initial tranche at current price** | **0–0.5%** — do not initiate a full position at $219.64 |
| **Conditional initiation** | **0.5% after Q3 confirms CV ≥2.5–3%** and FY26 guide is intact |
| **Add-to target** | **1.0–1.25%** on a pullback to $180–190 or on CV >3% with a credible FY27 guide |
| **Existing holders** | **Hold; cap at 1.5%.** If above 1.5%, reduce to 1.5% into strength. |

### Rationale

- **Kelly logic:** The probability-weighted intrinsic value is ~$253, implying ~15% upside. The bear case is ~$129, or −41%. With 62% annualised volatility, the edge is thin relative to the dispersion. A half-Kelly allocation for a 1–1.5% edge-to-risk ratio is roughly **0.5–1.0%**, not a 3–5% position.
- **Risk budget:** A 1% position with 62% volatility contributes ~0.62% of portfolio volatility. A 25–27% stop-loss on a 1% position costs ~0.25–0.27% of portfolio — acceptable for a diversifying, low-correlation name, but not for a larger bet.
- **Liquidity:** ~1.2M shares/day (~$260M notional). A 1% position in a $1B portfolio is ~$10M, under 5% of ADV. In a multi-billion portfolio, scale entries over 3–5 days with VWAP/limit orders.
- **Governance/litigation cap:** Non-Fin Risk HIGH and Geo Legal MEDIUM justify a hard cap below what pure valuation would suggest. The CLO departure and class action are not priced as a specific reserve; a derivative suit or adverse disclosure could compress the multiple again.

**Bottom line:** 1.0% target, 1.5% max, 0.5% starter only after confirmation. At $219.64, new capital should **pass** unless the investor is willing to own a 0.5% “event stub” into the print.

---

## 4. Portfolio Fit Analysis

### Sector concentration

- FMP classifies IT as “Technology,” but economically it is **information services / research & advisory**, not semis or hardware. The correct peer set is FDS, MORN, VRSK, FORR, CLVT, not NVDA/AAPL/MSFT.
- If the portfolio is already overweight **data & analytics** (FDS, MORN, VRSK), adding IT increases a correlated information-services exposure: IT–FDS correlation 0.68, IT–MORN 0.65, IT–VRSK 0.58. In that case, keep IT at the low end (0.5–1.0%) or pass.
- If the portfolio is overweight **mega-cap tech/semis**, IT does **not** add semiconductor beta. Its correlation with SPY is only 0.07 and beta is 0.31. It adds idiosyncratic AI-sentiment risk, not broad tech beta.

### Factor exposure

| Factor | IT’s contribution | Portfolio implication |
|---|---|---|
| **Value** | Positive — cheapest in its peer set on P/E and FCF yield | Adds value tilt; helpful if portfolio is growth-heavy |
| **Quality** | Positive but deteriorating — ROIC ~26%, down from ~33%; operating margin 15.8% FY25 | Adds quality, but not stable quality |
| **Momentum** | Negative — 12-1 momentum −23.5%, despite +55.7% 3M | Contrarian value exposure; could be a drag if momentum persists |
| **Low volatility** | Strongly negative — 61.9% annualised vol, −77% cycle drawdown | Increases portfolio tail risk; size accordingly |
| **Size** | Mid-cap ~$14B | Minor size tilt; liquid enough |

**Net:** IT is a **value/quality name with negative momentum and high idiosyncratic volatility**. It is not a defensive compounder despite its low beta. The low beta is misleading: R² is 0.005, so market beta explains almost none of its risk. Diversification benefit is limited in an AI/growth scare because IT’s drawdowns are narrative-driven, not market-driven.

### Correlation considerations

| Pair | 252-day correlation |
|---|---:|
| IT–SPY | 0.07 |
| IT–FDS | 0.68 |
| IT–MORN | 0.65 |
| IT–VRSK | 0.58 |
| IT–FORR | 0.43 |

IT is a **portfolio diversifier versus the broad market but a concentrator versus information-services peers**. Cap it at 1.0–1.5% and avoid pairing it with large FDS/MORN/VRSK positions unless the portfolio is deliberately running a data-analytics bucket.

---

## 5. Entry Strategy

### Do not buy the print at $219.64

The stock is:
- +75% off the June 2026 low;
- +55.7% over three months and +19.8% over one month;
- above the median sell-side target of ~$189–200;
- trading above every major moving average;
- heading into a binary Q3 print on 3-Nov-2026 with consensus EPS $2.84 and revenue $1.487B.

The fundamental setup is improving — CV accelerated in Q2, the UBS channel check is above consensus, and Gartner has beaten 7/7 quarters — but the **entry point is poor**. A beat is likely; a beat that is already priced is not a reason to buy.

### Scale-in plan

| Tranche | Size | Trigger |
|---|---:|---|
| **1** | **0.5%** | After Q3 (3-Nov): CV growth ≥2.5% (prefer ≥3%), client count stabilises near/above 12,775, FY26 revenue/EPS guide intact, no adverse legal disclosure. |
| **2** | **0.5%** | Pullback to $180–190 **or** CV >3% with FY27 revenue growth guided ≥3%. |
| **3** | **0.25–0.5%** | After Feb-2027 FY26 results/initial FY27 guide: revenue growth ≥3%, operating margin ≥20%, buyback sustainable within FCF. |

**If price runs above $240 before confirmation:** do not chase. Wait for the Feb-2027 guide or a pullback. The Growth Researcher’s trim zone starts at $240 without a 2027 guide.

**If Q3 shows CV <2%, client count below ~12,500, or a FY27 revenue guide down >3%:** pass and revisit at $150–165.

---

## 6. Risk Management Rules

### Stop-loss

- **Hard stop:** closing price below **$160–165** (approximately −25% to −27%). This is below the August breakout base (~$170–180) and inside the macro bear-case zone of $150–165.
- Use a **closing basis**, not intraday, given 62% volatility and repeated 20%+ single-day gaps. Position sizing — not the stop — is the primary risk control.
- For a 1% position, a stop at $165 risks ~0.25% of portfolio. That is acceptable. Do not widen the stop to “give it room”; if the thesis is right, it should not retest the June panic zone.

### Thesis invalidation conditions

Exit or reassess immediately if any of the following occur:

1. **CV growth falls below 2% for two consecutive quarters**, or turns negative.
2. **Client count falls below ~12,500** — the current 12,775 is already down 4.5% y/y; further attrition confirms price-led growth on a shrinking base.
3. **FY27 revenue guided down more than 3%**, or management withdraws the CV/guidance framework.
4. **Operating margin fails to hold ~20% in 2027** — the current margin recovery is cost-cut-driven; a 2027 margin cliff would break the EPS story.
5. **Buyback is paused or net leverage exceeds ~2.5x** — the buyback is the main EPS engine; a pause removes the floor.
6. **Adverse legal/governance development:** derivative suit naming directors, SEC inquiry into AI-related disclosures, auditor change, or evidence that the CLO departure relates to disclosure-control disagreements.
7. **AI-attributed contract-value churn is disclosed** — e.g., renewal rates or seat counts materially deteriorating because of LLM substitution.

### Trim triggers

| Trigger | Action |
|---|---|
| **$240–250 with no CV >3% or FY27 guide** | Trim one-third |
| **$255–265** (≈90% of base-case intrinsic value of $286) | Trim half |
| **$290–300** | Exit/avoid unless CV >5% and FY27 guide supports a higher terminal value |
| **Position exceeds 1.5% of portfolio** | Rebalance to 1.5% |

### Event-risk protocol

- **Before 3-Nov:** no new full position. If already holding, consider hedging or trimming to 0.5–1.0% if the position is above target.
- **After 3-Nov:** re-underwrite within 48 hours. The key numbers are CV growth, net new CV, client count, and FY26/FY27 guide — not the EPS beat.
- **Feb-2027:** the highest-variance event. Initial FY27 guidance at this meeting took the stock down 21% in Feb-2026. Size the position so a −20% gap is tolerable.

---

## 7. Final Portfolio Action

### **HOLD existing positions. PASS on new capital at $219.64.**

- **Existing holders:** Hold at 0.5–1.5%, cap at 1.5%, trim into $240–265 strength, and use $160–165 as the hard stop. Do not add before Q3.
- **New capital:** Pass at the current price. The stock is a fairly priced, high-quality franchise with a 13% discount to intrinsic value — not the 25–30% margin of safety required given HIGH governance/litigation risk, 62% volatility, negative momentum, and a binary print.
- **Conditional initiate:** 0.5% only after Q3 confirms CV ≥2.5–3% and the guide is intact; add to 1.0–1.25% on a pullback to $180–190 or on CV >3% with a credible FY27 outlook.

**One-line portfolio view:** *Gartner is a good business at a fair price with a bad entry point and a live governance overhang. Own it small if you already own it; do not chase it; buy the confirmation or the pullback, not the narrative.*

---

**Data gaps / caveats:** Peer valuation multiples are unreliable — FMP’s “Technology” peer set returns mega-cap semis/hardware, not information-services comparables. Segment-level revenue/margin mix and the debt maturity schedule were not retrievable. The 10-K/10-Q legal-proceedings note and DEF 14A could not be pulled directly, so litigation reserves and governance details rely on secondary sources. Insider transaction direction was unavailable. The provider’s market cap ($15.8B) uses 72.1M diluted shares versus the ~63–66M current share count used by several agents; valuation ratios should be treated as a range, not a point estimate.

**Sector:** Information Services / IT Research & Advisory (FMP classifies IT within "Technology")

This is the single most important judgement in this brief.

### 1. Sector Overview

Gartner sits in the IT research & advisory industry — a roughly $15–20B global niche inside the far larger information-services complex, where vendors sell subscription access to proprietary analysis, benchmarks and expert inquiry (Research), plus conferences and bespoke consulting. It is a **structural oligopoly with collapsing barriers to entry**: Gartner holds an estimated >50% share of IT research/advisory and is ~16x Forrester's revenue, but the industry's core product — a written report synthesising expert opinion — is precisely what generative AI now produces at near-zero marginal cost. The defining feature of 2026 is a **sharp divergence between end-market demand and business-model viability**: Gartner's own forecast has worldwide IT spending growing **+14.2% to $6.37trn in 2026** (revised up from +10.8% and then +13.5% during the year) with AI spending **+49.5% to $2.7trn**, yet the information-services equities de-rated violently on AI-disruption fear. Sector cycle position: **late-mature, entering structural disruption** — not a normal cyclical downturn, and therefore not something an IT-budget recovery will fix.

### 2. Key Tailwinds

- **An unambiguous IT budget boom in the end market.** Gartner's July-2026 forecast puts worldwide IT spend at **$6.37trn, +14.2%** — upgraded three times in 2026 (+10.8% → +13.5% → +14.2%). AI spending at $2.7trn (+49.5%). Rising budget and, critically, rising *architectural complexity* (AI platforms, neoclouds, agentic tooling) is the raw feedstock for advisory demand: buyers cannot evaluate this category unaided.
- **AI is expanding inquiry volume, not just cannibalising content.** Gartner's 1Q26 evidence is that AI-related inquiry is a net demand *driver* — clients need help with AI governance, EU AI Act compliance, vendor selection and cost optimisation. Gartner's own research output (the "80% of neoclouds extinct by 2030" call, which moved CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN) demonstrates the brand still sets industry narrative — a durable pricing asset.
- **Conferences and consulting are counter-cyclical and margin-rich.** The IT Symposium/Xpo franchise is filling on AI themes, and consulting/cost-optimisation work historically *rises* when clients tighten budgets. Meanwhile buybacks cut diluted shares from 86.2M (2021) to 72.1M (2025), ~16% cumulative, mechanically supporting EPS.

### 3. Key Headwinds

- **Contract value growth has decelerated to stall speed.** Q3-2026 contract value growth of **~+2.5%** (UBS, vs 2.3% consensus) and net new CV of only **~$58M/quarter** — against mid-to-high single digits historically. The shares are ~62% below the Feb-2025 peak of $584. The market has re-priced the entire "sell expert opinion by the seat" model, and it has not restored the multiple despite the operating results holding up.
- **Seat rationalisation and margin erosion.** Enterprise procurement is consolidating read-only seats — the lowest-value tier — while Gartner defends the franchise by reinvesting in AI tooling and restructuring. Operating margin has compressed **-515bp in two years (20.9% FY23 → 15.8% FY25)** and gross margin from 69.5% to 67.7%.
